claude.country: United States, UAE, Jordan (multi-country registry cohorts)

links.outcome: Discrimination of GVHD models on external validation cohorts versus internal validation
links.effect: Internal AUROC 0.63 (acute) and 0.72 (chronic); external AUROC 0.51–0.57 (acute) and 0.54–0.64 (chronic); external C-indices 0.47–0.53 vs training 0.679.
links.quote: External validation demonstrated AUROC ranges of 0.51–0.57 (acute) and 0.54–0.64 (chronic), with consistent performance across disease subgroups despite substantial heterogeneity in transplant practices and feature availability.

links.outcome: Calibration drift across external cohorts requiring local recalibration
links.effect: Negative calibration intercept (risk overestimation) in 10 of 11 evaluable external cohort-target combinations, with heterogeneous slope drift requiring cohort-specific recalibration.
links.quote: Calibration analysis identified systematic external risk overestimation (negative calibration intercept in 10 of 11 evaluable external cohort-target combinations) with heterogeneous slope drift requiring cohort-specific recalibration.

links.outcome: Model performance generalization to new external populations
links.effect: External AUROC fell to 0.51–0.57 for acute GVHD and 0.54–0.64 for chronic GVHD, with calibration overestimation in 10 of 11 combinations.
links.quote: Per-cohort recalibration is required before clinical deployment, with prospective validation and benchmarking against established GVHD risk scores identified as priority next steps.
